The home mountain of the Greek Gods is Mount Olympus.

To understand the concept of search engines using the provided analogy, imagine the Internet as a massive, chaotic library that never stops growing. In this library, every website is a unique book, and every individual web page is a single page within that book. Without a system to organize these books, finding a specific piece of information would be like trying to read every book in the library from cover to cover to find one specific sentence.

This is where a search engine like Google acts as the library’s master index or catalog system. Instead of forcing you to browse every shelf, you simply tell the index what you are looking for. The search engine then scans its records to point you directly to the specific "book" (website) and the exact "page" (web page) that contains the answer you need, saving you from having to manually search through the entire collection.
